speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your infant's recurrent stridor and wheezing, please tell me their age and exactly what activity triggers these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia. The combination of stridor worsening with feeding and neck flexion, along with vomiting, is highly characteristic of this condition caused by the collapse of supraglottic tissues during inspiration.
